content.comment_body: I inserted an SD card that was incorrectly formatted (used for Raspberry Pi). After trying a new card and performing factory resets, the device still only displays a screen like this. Is there a deeper firmware reload option that could resolve the issue? [article_no] [product_name] ([company_name] only)

Thread closed due to duplicate question. The second topic titled 'Did I break my [product_name]? Only showing open source license' is published within the conference for [product_name] - Software. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: User experienced a startup issue with the [product_name] following use of an incorrectly formatted SD card intended for Raspberry Pi. After attempts to resolve the problem with a new card and factory reset, the device continues to display only an open source license screen rather than operating normally. This case illustrates uncertainty about available recovery steps when a device encounters faults due to incompatible accessories.
analysis.user_expectations: User hopes to restore full device functionality after accidentally using an SD card with the wrong format, seeking an advanced firmware reload method to recover proper operation.
pain_keywords: device stuck on open source license
inability to recover via factory reset
